props.title: Sunset Boulevard
props.initialSlug: Faded star lures writer into her delusional world

sections.content: Sunset Boulevard (1950) stands as Billy Wilder's masterful noir about Hollywood's dark underbelly, told through the eyes of dead screenwriter Joe Gillis floating in a pool. Gloria Swanson's portrayal of faded silent film star Norma Desmond defined the "forgotten actress" archetype that influenced films like Whatever Happened to Baby Jane? (1962) and Mulholland Drive (2001). The film's cynical take on Hollywood's treatment of aging stars and disposal of talent remains painfully relevant, while its innovative narrative structure - opening with the protagonist's death - inspired countless films like American Beauty (1999).

movies.title: The Artist
movies.slug: This Oscar-winning silent film pays homage to Hollywood's transition from silent to sound pictures

sections.content: Wilder's direction masterfully blends film noir elements with Hollywood satire, creating a unique "noir about the movies." The decrepit Desmond mansion, shot by John F. Seitz with dramatic shadows and decay, became a template for depicting Old Hollywood gothic. This visual style influenced films like Ed Wood (1994) and The Day of the Locust (1975). The film's meta-commentary includes real silent film stars like Buster Keaton appearing as Norma's "waxworks" bridge partners, adding authentic tragedy to its exploration of fame's fleeting nature.

The screenplay by Wilder, Charles Brackett, and D.M. Marshman Jr. crafted unforgettable lines ("I am big. It's the pictures that got small.") that encapsulate Hollywood's cruel relationship with aging stars. This theme resonates through later works like Maps to the Stars (2014) and Once Upon a Time in Hollywood (2019), showing how little has changed in the industry's treatment of fading celebrities. movies.title: Mank
movies.slug: David Fincher's examination of 1930s Hollywood through the eyes of Citizen Kane screenwriter Herman J. Mankiewicz

sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond Hollywood critique into psychological character studies. Norma Desmond's descent into delusion inspired complex character portraits in films like Black Swan (2010) and Birdman (2014). The power dynamic between Norma and Joe influenced later explorations of toxic relationships in Hollywood, seen in Swimming with Sharks (1994) and The Devil Wears Prada (2006).
